incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: GPU OOM during prefill -> container restart on gpu-node-22. Model=redwood/long-context-v2@v12. Count=1 container restart, impact=degraded responses. Incident ID=INC-2190012378. See traces: https://internal/trace/2190012378

maya (ops-oncall): taking pager. I'm on-call and will triage. Can someone post the pod name and recent logs?

ben (eng-runtime): pulling logs now. likely prefill OOM (large prompt/context). Run: `kubectl -n prod logs pod/longctx-runtime-7f8k -c runtime | tail -n 200`

sara.p: flagging customer teams — Lucas, can you confirm whether any customers reported errors?

lucas (customer-success): I see 3 support tickets referencing increased error rate from customers on the long-context route. One is high-priority (enterprise).

anil.m: snippet from logs I grabbed a minute ago:
```
2026-03-15T21:14:02Z runtime ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T21:14:02Z runtime INFO: prefill tokens=183456, kv-cache bytes requested=18.2GB
2026-03-15T21:14:02Z runtime FATAL: container restarting due to uncaught exception
```

kai.h: that's consistent with prefill trying to allocate KV cache for huge prompt. We should enable prefill trimming and fallback to smaller model concurrently. I propose: 1) route traffic for long-context-v2 -> long-context-v1-small (compatible) 2) set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=200000 on runtime env or enable trim mode `PREFILL_TRIM=1` 3) cordon gpu-node-22 and restart affected pod.

maya (ops-oncall): executing step 1 now — updating routing to fallback model (canary 100% for the cluster).

pagerduty: :bell: Pager duty note: alert acknowledged by maya. Escalation level 1.

ben (eng-runtime): I'll prepare hotpatch. Quick mitigation patch (runtime): `PREFILL_TRIM_ENABLED=true; PREFILL_TRIM_THRESHOLD=150000` and bump prefill memory guard. I'll push a rollout to the runtime group and roll 1 replica to test.

maya (ops-oncall): cordoning node gpu-node-22: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-22` — succeeded. Draining pods and restarting runtime pod now.

sara.p: also set temporary rate-limit for long-context route to reduce burstiness. Doing that now.

kai.h: sample command I ran in staging to enable trim without restart: `kubectl set env ds/runtime PREFILL_TRIM_ENABLED=true --namespace=prod` but we should prefer a rolling restart to pick up kernel flags. Ben, do you want me to apply the env change or you push the image?

ben (eng-runtime): apply env var first for a single deployment patch `kubectl patch deployment/longctx-runtime -n prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"PREFILL_TRIM_ENABLED","value":"true"},{"name":"PREFILL_TRIM_THRESHOLD","value":"150000"}] }]}}}}'` — then rolling restart. I'll monitor memory.

maya (ops-oncall): pod restarted and came back up. Container logs after restart show prefill trimming engaged:
```
2026-03-15T21:16:40Z runtime INFO: PREFILL_TRIM_ENABLED=true
2026-03-15T21:16:42Z runtime INFO: incoming prefill tokens=183456, trimmed to=150000
2026-03-15T21:16:42Z runtime INFO: kv-cache bytes allocated=14.7GB
2026-03-15T21:16:45Z runtime INFO: request served successfully
```

lucas (customer-success): support update: initial reports resolved for 2 customers after traffic shift. One enterprise customer still seeing failures — routed them to support channel and opened a ticket to SRE/AM.

anil.m: quick note re root cause: the model variant v12 uses larger KV per token (architectural change) and our prefill guard was not updated. Prefill requests with concatenated user history produced >170k tokens for some requests, exceeding allocated GPU memory on this node.

ben (eng-runtime): confirmed. We need permanent fixes: 1) enforce PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS at edge / router 2) add runtime backpressure to reject prefill > X tokens with clear error for customers 3) add per-model KV size metadata to routing so the router calculates estimated GPU memory per request.

sara.p: customer-impact summary for Slack: "12:14–12:26 UTC degraded responses and 502s for long-context-v2. ~7 customer requests failed across 3 customers, highest impact on 1 enterprise customer. Mitigated by 12:16 UTC with routing+trim."

pagerduty: :white_check_mark: Alert resolved by maya at 2190012812.

maya (ops-oncall): handing off to Ben for full postmortem and follow-ups. Ben, please own the action items: update runtime guards, router validation, and add model KV metadata. I'll re-open if we see recurrence.

ben (eng-runtime): taking ownership. Timeline:
- 2190012378 Root alert (incident-bot)
- 2190012391 Maya ack + cordon
- 2190012410 Ben set trimming env + restart
- 2190012460 Pod back healthy, router fallback applied
- 2190012812 Incident marked resolved (routing+trim mitigations)

anil.m: tagging for postmortem: root-cause=insufficient prefill guard for v12 model kv growth; contributing=traffic burst + large user conversations. Proposed next-steps: router-level prefill token cap (50k default), model-specific kv footprint in model registry, alerting on per-node gpu memory pressure from runtime metrics.

lucas (customer-success): I'll send a proactive customer update and include mitigation & timeline.

ben (eng-runtime): will open INC-2190012378-postmortem and assign action items with owners and deadlines. Thanks everyone for quick coordination.

sara.p: adding follow-up: update docs for "prefill trimming" and communicate to solutions engineers.

incident-bot: Note: channel archived snapshot saved to /incidents/snapshots/2190012378.txt

maya (ops-oncall): end of thread — handoff complete.
